fixes.explanation: That's it. Abraham complained to Abimelech "…about a well that Abimelech’s servants had seized…" (Genesis 21:25) The servants took the well, and Abraham brought his complaint to the king. Picture someone eating the last cookie you were saving, and you're the one walking up to the boss about it. Abraham just took it straight to the top.

Yes, Beersheba. The text says the place "…was called Beersheba, because it was there that the two of them swore an oath." (Genesis 21:31) The name comes from what happened right on that spot. It's like a bakery named after the first batch that ever came out of its oven. You hear the name, and you know the story.

problems.problem: The joke compares guarding a well to guarding a chocolate chip, but Abraham's action is complaining about a well that was seized, not guarding it.
The price-sticker joke refers to Papa Dorin's backstory without explaining that the sticker was on him. It also compares a place named after an oath to an unrelated price sticker.
